operations_plan.summary: Establish the fan-facing +X positional convention, derive a port standard from the existing lower-left fittings, and consolidate the existing fitting pair to prepare one bottom-left inlet location.

steps.description: Use the semantic fan-facing +X view as the controlling orientation for all positional references. Establish projected top, bottom, left, and right limits from the rounded rectangular perimeter frame. Identify the requested bottom-left and top-right regions from this view rather than from the mirrored branded -X view. The exact coordinate signs of the visual left and right sides must be verified in the CAD workspace because the view projection can reverse the displayed Z direction.

Inspect the two gold-colored fittings at the visual bottom-left of the +X view and extract their center axes, attachment points, maximum outside diameter, neck diameter, projection length, barb or flare profile, bore diameter if present, and root fillet size. No port dimensions or fitting standard were supplied, so use these measured values as the governing standard for both requested ports. If the existing B-spline solids do not contain measurable bores, infer a manufacturable concentric bore while retaining sufficient neck wall thickness.

Select the lower of the two existing fittings in the fan-facing +X view as the bottom-left inlet reference; this is expected to be FEAT_LOWER_PORT, face 795, solid 16. Remove the adjacent upper fitting, expected to be FEAT_UPPER_PORT, face 794, solid 15, and heal or locally rebuild its former attachment area into a continuous side-tank wall. This consolidation avoids leaving two ambiguous connections at the inlet corner. The solid-to-feature correspondence and whether either fitting already penetrates the coolant tank are unresolved and must be confirmed before deletion.

Create parametric variables from the measured fitting geometry for port outside diameter, bore diameter, root diameter, projection length, barb length, flare diameter, root fillet, and minimum corner clearance. Reuse this single parameter set for both inlet and outlet so the connections have a consistent hose interface. Record that the connection standard remains unresolved beyond matching the supplied model geometry.

operations_plan.summary: Create or reconstruct one functional coolant inlet at the bottom-left corner in the fan-facing +X view and connect it through the local tank wall.

steps.description: Locate the outer side-tank wall at the visual bottom-left corner of the +X view. Use the retained lower fitting center and axis from OP_001 as the preferred inlet centerline. If the retained fitting is unsuitable, place the center on the nearest planar or locally tangent side-tank patch while preserving its existing edge offsets. Confirm that the center lies in the coolant-containing tank rather than over the fin-and-tube core, lower frame rail, or a closed structural web. The exact tank-wall face is unresolved within the grouped perimeter faces 15-62 and must be selected by geometric adjacency.

Create a datum plane normal to the inlet centerline at the selected side-tank attachment point. On this plane, sketch concentric circles for the neck outside diameter and coolant bore using the parameters established in OP_001. Constrain the circles concentric with the retained fitting axis and constrain the center to the selected tank-wall reference point.

Cut the inner circular profile through the full local tank-wall thickness and terminate it at the connected internal coolant volume. Do not allow the cut to extend into the active core slab, core edge strips, lower frame rail, or fan structure. Verify the cut creates one continuous hydraulic opening and does not leave a blind cavity.

Reconstruct the inlet as a hollow outward-projecting hose neck. Either reuse and boolean-union solid 16 to the tank or revolve/extrude a new annular neck and matching barb profile about the inlet axis using the measured fitting parameters. Ensure the neck projects outward from the radiator envelope, away from the core and fans. Union the neck to the tank and maintain the concentric bore through the complete fitting.

Add a smooth root fillet or blended reinforcement where the inlet neck joins the tank, matching the existing fitting style and avoiding excessive encroachment into the lower rail. Apply a small lead-in chamfer or rounded lip at the hose end only if it is consistent with the measured reference fitting. Designate the completed new geometry as the bottom-left coolant inlet.

operations_plan.summary: Create a matching coolant outlet at the top-right corner in the fan-facing +X view and connect it to the opposite tank volume.

steps.description: Identify the visual top-right side-tank region in the fan-facing +X view. Establish the nominal outlet center by diagonally mirroring the completed inlet center across the projected center of the radiator frame, thereby preserving comparable offsets from the top and right frame boundaries. Confirm the candidate point is on a coolant-containing tank wall and not on the fin core, top cap neck, central bridge, or a closed structural rail.

Check radial and axial clearance between the nominal outlet envelope and the upper-right diagonal mounting boss, top service cap, frame corner transitions, core edge, and fan guard. Keep both mount solid 17 and cap solid 19 unchanged. If the nominal mirrored position interferes, translate the outlet center only along the available upper-right tank wall by the minimum distance required to clear the preserved components while remaining recognizably in the top-right region. No numerical clearance was specified, so use at least the inlet root-filleted envelope plus normal manufacturing separation.

Create a datum plane normal to the outward direction of the selected top-right tank wall. Sketch concentric outlet neck and bore circles using the same diameters as the completed inlet. Orient the outlet axis outward from the top-right side of the assembly; it should oppose the inlet's outward direction when the ports occupy opposite side tanks. The precise local face and projection vector are unresolved until the grouped frame faces are inspected.

Cut the outlet bore through the complete local tank-wall thickness until it intersects the internal coolant volume. Limit the cut so it does not intersect the top rail, fill-cap neck, active radiator core, fan guard, or upper-right mount. Confirm that the new opening is hydraulically continuous and is not blocked by an internal closure web.

Create the hollow outlet neck by reusing the inlet's parametric annular neck and barb profile. Revolve or extrude it along the outlet axis, trim its root to the local tank surface, and boolean-union it to the tank. Preserve a constant open bore from the hose end into the internal coolant volume. Match the inlet's outside diameter, bore, projection length, barb geometry, and wall thickness unless local clearance requires shortening only the projection length.

Apply the same root fillet and hose-end treatment used on the inlet, adjusted only as necessary to remain clear of the preserved mount and top cap. Designate the completed top-right connection as the coolant outlet.

operations_plan.summary: Validate the edited radiator for hydraulic continuity, geometric integrity, required port placement, and preservation of all unaffected components.

Remove sliver faces or invalid edges produced by tank-wall healing and port-root trimming.

Inspect the completed assembly from the fan-facing +X direction and verify that exactly one designated inlet occupies the bottom-left region and one designated outlet occupies the top-right region. Also inspect from the side and top views to verify that both fittings project outward with usable hose engagement and do not point into the frame or fan envelopes.

Verify preservation of the radiator core and fin envelope, both seven-blade fan modules, fan hubs and guards, central support, top and bottom frame rails, top fill cap, both diagonal mounting bosses, and all unaffected visible surfaces. Confirm adequate static clearance between the new ports and the fan guards, mount bosses, cap, and installation envelope.

Perform a coolant-path connectivity check between the bottom-left inlet and top-right outlet. Confirm that both openings communicate through the radiator's coolant passages. Do not introduce internal partitions unless inspection proves that the existing tank arrangement prevents communication; internal routing and pass configuration were not specified by the request.

operations_plan.summary: Create or reconstruct one functional coolant inlet at the bottom-left corner in the fan-facing +X view and connect it through the local tank wall.

steps.description: Locate the outer side-tank wall at the visual bottom-left corner of the +X view. Use the retained lower fitting center and axis from OP_001 as the preferred inlet centerline. If the retained fitting is unsuitable, place the center on the nearest planar or locally tangent side-tank patch while preserving its existing edge offsets. Confirm that the center lies in the coolant-containing tank rather than over the fin-and-tube core, lower frame rail, or a closed structural web. The exact tank-wall face is unresolved within the grouped perimeter faces 15-62 and must be selected by geometric adjacency.

Create a datum plane normal to the inlet centerline at the selected side-tank attachment point. On this plane, sketch concentric circles for the neck outside diameter and coolant bore using the parameters established in OP_001. Constrain the circles concentric with the retained fitting axis and constrain the center to the selected tank-wall reference point.

Cut the inner circular profile through the full local tank-wall thickness and terminate it at the connected internal coolant volume. Do not allow the cut to extend into the active core slab, core edge strips, lower frame rail, or fan structure. Verify the cut creates one continuous hydraulic opening and does not leave a blind cavity.

Reconstruct the inlet as a hollow outward-projecting hose neck. Either reuse and boolean-union solid 16 to the tank or revolve/extrude a new annular neck and matching barb profile about the inlet axis using the measured fitting parameters. Ensure the neck projects outward from the radiator envelope, away from the core and fans. Union the neck to the tank and maintain the concentric bore through the complete fitting.

Add a smooth root fillet or blended reinforcement where the inlet neck joins the tank, matching the existing fitting style and avoiding excessive encroachment into the lower rail. Apply a small lead-in chamfer or rounded lip at the hose end only if it is consistent with the measured reference fitting. Designate the completed new geometry as the bottom-left coolant inlet.

operations_plan.summary: Create a matching coolant outlet at the top-right corner in the fan-facing +X view and connect it to the opposite tank volume.

steps.description: Identify the visual top-right side-tank region in the fan-facing +X view. Establish the nominal outlet center by diagonally mirroring the completed inlet center across the projected center of the radiator frame, thereby preserving comparable offsets from the top and right frame boundaries. Confirm the candidate point is on a coolant-containing tank wall and not on the fin core, top cap neck, central bridge, or a closed structural rail.

Check radial and axial clearance between the nominal outlet envelope and the upper-right diagonal mounting boss, top service cap, frame corner transitions, core edge, and fan guard. Keep both mount solid 17 and cap solid 19 unchanged. If the nominal mirrored position interferes, translate the outlet center only along the available upper-right tank wall by the minimum distance required to clear the preserved components while remaining recognizably in the top-right region. No numerical clearance was specified, so use at least the inlet root-filleted envelope plus normal manufacturing separation.

Create a datum plane normal to the outward direction of the selected top-right tank wall. Sketch concentric outlet neck and bore circles using the same diameters as the completed inlet. Orient the outlet axis outward from the top-right side of the assembly; it should oppose the inlet's outward direction when the ports occupy opposite side tanks. The precise local face and projection vector are unresolved until the grouped frame faces are inspected.

Cut the outlet bore through the complete local tank-wall thickness until it intersects the internal coolant volume. Limit the cut so it does not intersect the top rail, fill-cap neck, active radiator core, fan guard, or upper-right mount. Confirm that the new opening is hydraulically continuous and is not blocked by an internal closure web.

Create the hollow outlet neck by reusing the inlet's parametric annular neck and barb profile. Revolve or extrude it along the outlet axis, trim its root to the local tank surface, and boolean-union it to the tank. Preserve a constant open bore from the hose end into the internal coolant volume. Match the inlet's outside diameter, bore, projection length, barb geometry, and wall thickness unless local clearance requires shortening only the projection length.

Apply the same root fillet and hose-end treatment used on the inlet, adjusted only as necessary to remain clear of the preserved mount and top cap. Designate the completed top-right connection as the coolant outlet.

operations_plan.summary: Validate the edited radiator for hydraulic continuity, geometric integrity, required port placement, and preservation of all unaffected components.

steps.description: Run a solid-validity and interference check after all booleans. Confirm that the inlet and outlet are watertight unions with the corresponding tank walls, each has one unobstructed bore into the coolant volume, and no residual opening remains where the redundant lower-left fitting was removed. Remove sliver faces or invalid edges produced by tank-wall healing and port-root trimming.

Inspect the completed assembly from the fan-facing +X direction and verify that exactly one designated inlet occupies the bottom-left region and one designated outlet occupies the top-right region. Also inspect from the side and top views to verify that both fittings project outward with usable hose engagement and do not point into the frame or fan envelopes.

Verify preservation of the radiator core and fin envelope, both seven-blade fan modules, fan hubs and guards, central support, top and bottom frame rails, top fill cap, both diagonal mounting bosses, and all unaffected visible surfaces. Confirm adequate static clearance between the new ports and the fan guards, mount bosses, cap, and installation envelope.

Perform a coolant-path connectivity check between the bottom-left inlet and top-right outlet. Confirm that both openings communicate through the radiator's coolant passages. Do not introduce internal partitions unless inspection proves that the existing tank arrangement prevents communication; internal routing and pass configuration were not specified by the request.
